domain: workspace store (src/lib/workspace.tsx) — ACTIONS. The single React context that backs every "enterprise app" in the product: Marketplace installs, AI credits, artifacts, agent runs, approvals, audit trail, companies, guardrails, runners, connectors, client portal, compliance registers, Travel & Expense, Support & Ticketing, IT Asset Management, Pitch Pilot, Sales & POS, generic CRM/HR records and schedules. Every one of the 87 public mutation methods is a synchronous localStorage write: the file contains zero fetch, zero async, zero await and zero setTimeout. One global browser key, 'apragya.workspace' (line 68), holds the entire blob. No tenant id and no user id appears anywhere in the key or the payload, even though src/lib/auth.tsx already has a real server session with `activeTenantId` and `tenants[]` — so switching tenant, switching account, or opening the app in another browser silently shows the wrong data or no data. NONE of the mutations are tenant scoped and NONE are user scoped.

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Every mutation below funnels through this: setState((prev) => {...}) and, INSIDE the updater, localStorage.setItem('apragya.workspace', JSON.stringify(wholeBlob)). One global key, no tenant id and no user id in the key or the payload. The whole tenant — every ticket, asset, invoice, audit row — is re-serialised and rewritten on every keystroke-level change. The try/catch at 943-947 swallows QuotaExceededError and SecurityError with the comment 'state stays in memory for this session', so a failed save is indistinguishable from a successful one in the UI. Writing inside the setState updater also means React StrictMode runs the write twice in dev, and the whole file contains zero fetch, zero async, zero await and zero setTimeout.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Delete this primitive. Each mutation becomes its own authenticated call to the API, scoped by tenant_id taken from the httpOnly session cookie the server already issues (src/lib/auth.tsx), never from anything the browser supplies. Writes must be awaited, must surface failure, and must be rejected server-side when the caller is not a member of the tenant.
operations.apiMethodPath: n/a — replaced by per-resource endpoints below
operations.authorization: none today — any script on the origin can rewrite the entire tenant
operations.validation: none — no schema check on read or write
operations.sideEffect: rewrites the entire tenant document on every call

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. JSON.parse of one global key on mount (useEffect at 938). No key at all -> returns `empty`, i.e. a brand-new tenant with two pre-installed apps, five seeded guardrail policies, a 16-row data inventory and three fabricated audit rows. Any parse error -> silently returns `empty`, discarding everything the user had. Not tenant scoped and not user scoped: sign out, sign in as a different account or switch tenant with auth.switchTenant and this store keeps serving the previous tenant's records.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Server-side load per (tenant_id, resource), paginated, with 401/403 distinguished from 'empty'. A corrupt or missing payload must be an error state, never silently substituted with a fresh fake tenant. Tenant switching must invalidate and refetch every list.
operations.authorization: none today — reads whatever the browser holds regardless of who is signed in
operations.validation: `JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<Persisted>` — an unchecked cast; any shape is accepted

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Spreads the stored blob over `empty`, remaps 8 dead app codes through renamedCodes (line 879: CR->CRM, CM->CTR, IA/AP/PR->P2P, SL->POS, IN->INV, PY->PAY), re-adds the default app set for pre-v2 tenants, stamps version 2 and rewrites the key immediately (922-928). A one-level spread only: nested objects like teSettings/posSettings/supportSettings are taken wholesale from storage, so a tenant saved before a new nested field exists never receives its default and reads undefined.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Schema evolution belongs in versioned SQL migrations against the database, not in client code reading a browser key. The app-code renames become a one-time data migration on the installed_apps table.
operations.validation: no per-field validation; deep defaults are not merged
operations.sideEffect: rewrites the stored blob on first read after a version bump

operations.currentBehaviour: setState(read()) — re-reads the SAME browser's localStorage. Documented as picking up 'another tab's writes', which is all it can ever do: it cannot see another user, another device, or a server. Any 'Refresh' control wired to it is, today, a no-op-with-extra-steps for everyone but a second tab.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Re-issue the authenticated GET for the resource(s) on screen and replace cached state with the server's answer.

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {id: crypto.randomUUID(), title, body, at: now, read: false} and hard-truncates with .slice(0, 50) — notification 51 silently destroys the oldest row with no archive. No recipient field: a 'notification' nobody in particular receives, visible only in the browser that created it.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a notification row with recipient_user_id, tenant_id, type and payload; fan out server-side; keep history and paginate rather than truncating at 50.
operations.authorization: server-issued only; clients should not be able to mint arbitrary notifications for themselves
operations.validation: none — title and body are unvalidated free text
operations.sideEffect: destroys the 51st-oldest notification

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Pushes an app code onto an array (idempotent by early return), writes an 'app.installed' audit row and a notification reading '<App> has been installed successfully.' Nothing is provisioned: no entitlement, no billing check, no APP_QUOTA enforcement (the quota constant is exposed as appQuota but this function never consults it), no server record. Clear the browser and the app is uninstalled.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST an install that creates an installed_apps row for the tenant, checks the plan's app quota and entitlement, provisions the app's schema/defaults, and returns the persisted row before the UI claims success.
operations.authorization: org admin / owner only — currently any viewer can install anything
operations.validation: no quota check, no entitlement check, no plan check
operations.sideEffect: writes audit row + a success notification (see falseSuccessCopy)

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Array filter plus an 'app.uninstalled' audit row. The app's DATA is not touched — tickets, assets, POS docs all remain in the blob and reappear intact on reinstall. No confirmation, no cascade, no retention decision.
operations.requiredBehaviour: DELETE the installed_apps row; define explicitly whether the app's data is retained, soft-deleted or purged, and on what schedule.
operations.validation: no confirmation, no check for in-flight work in that app

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Membership toggle on a string array, audit row 'app.enabled'/'app.disabled'. Since nothing actually runs agents, disabling stops nothing — it only changes what the sidebar renders.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH installed_apps.disabled_at; the agent runtime must honour it as a hard gate before dispatching any run for that app.

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Compares against creditsLeft computed at line 1018 as MONTHLY_CREDITS(1000) - creditsUsed, returns false if short, otherwise increments a number in localStorage. This is the platform's entire billing enforcement — the file header calls the single credit pool 'the platform's defining rule'. A user can set creditsUsed to 0 in devtools and have unlimited credits. It also reads `creditsLeft` captured from the previous render, not from the updater's `prev`, so two calls in the same tick can both pass the check and overspend.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Credit debits must be a server-side transactional ledger: a credit_transactions table with an atomic balance check (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or a CHECK-constrained balance), an idempotency key per run, and the reset/top-up cadence made explicit. The client may display a balance; it must never be the one enforcing it.
operations.validation: stale-closure race on creditsLeft; no idempotency key; no negative/NaN guard on `credits`
operations.sideEffect: increments the only balance the product has

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Mints {id: crypto.randomUUID(), version: 1, status: 'draft', createdAt: now} and unshifts it, returning the object synchronously so callers can pretend they got a server response. No audit row is written (unlike almost every sibling). `skill` and `kind` are unvalidated free strings. No owner, no tenant.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST returning the persisted artifact with server-assigned id, tenant_id, created_by, and a real version chain.
operations.validation: name/skill/kind unvalidated; no uniqueness on name
operations.sideEffect: none — notably missing the audit row its siblings write

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES A RESULT: browser localStorage only — sets status to 'published' and does `version: artifact.version + 1`, an incremented counter standing in for a release. Nothing is deployed, validated, snapshotted or made callable; there is no published artifact anywhere. Re-publishing the same artifact keeps incrementing the number. No audit row, no publishedAt, no publisher.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a publish that snapshots the artifact definition into an immutable version row, runs validation, records publisher and published_at, and actually makes the artifact invocable. version must come from the version table, not from ++.
operations.authorization: publisher/approver role — currently anyone who can render the button
operations.validation: no pre-publish validation whatsoever
operations.sideEffect: increments a fake version counter

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES A RESULT: browser localStorage only. `const trace = sampleTrace` — the run's trace is the SAME six hard-coded steps imported from appData.ts (Intake/Enrich/Score/Policy check/Approval/Route, mentioning 'lead #4821' and 'Priya S.') for every run of every agent. status is hard-coded 'success' (the 'needs-review' and 'failed' variants in the Run type are unreachable here); credits (6) and ms (3260) are just sums over that canned array; the id is `run_` + Math.random().toString(36) — not even a uuid, and collision-prone. It then charges the tenant those fake credits via creditsUsed and writes an 'agent.run' audit row with status 'Success'. Runs are truncated to 25 with .slice(0, 25). No agent executes at any point.
operations.requiredBehaviour: A run must be created by the execution service: real trace steps with real node timings and token costs, a real terminal status, real credit debits through the ledger, and full history rather than the last 25. The client should only read runs.
operations.authorization: server-side only — a client must not be able to write run history or charge credits
operations.validation: none; `agent` and `source` are free strings with no FK
operations.sideEffect: charges 6 credits, writes a 'Success' audit row, discards the 26th-oldest run

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. One generic setter for four booleans — creditsAllocated, invitedTeammate, usedCopilot, dismissedChecklist — via a computed key. `invitedTeammate` is the worst offender: setting it ticks 'Invite a teammate' on the checklist while no invitation record exists and no email is sent. `creditsAllocated` likewise records no allocation. No audit row.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Delete the flags. 'Invited a teammate' must be derived from a real invitations row; 'allocated credits' from a real credit_allocations row; 'used copilot' from real usage telemetry. Only dismissedChecklist is legitimately a per-USER UI preference — and it belongs on the user, not the tenant.
operations.apiMethodPath: derive server-side; PATCH /users/me/preferences for the dismissal only
operations.validation: none — any of the four can be set to any value by the UI or devtools

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Writes 'pending' | 'on' | 'snoozed' into the tenant blob. SECURITY: the product's 2FA enrolment state is a string in a browser key the user fully controls — setting it to 'on' 'enables' two-factor with no enrolment, no secret, no verification and no effect on sign-in (src/lib/auth.tsx never consults it). No audit row for a security-state change.
operations.requiredBehaviour: 2FA belongs entirely to the auth service: enrolment with a verified TOTP secret or WebAuthn credential, per-USER not per-tenant, enforced at sign-in, with an audit row on every enrol/disable. This field must not exist in tenant state.
operations.validation: no verification step at all
operations.sideEffect: none — and that is the bug

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Maps read: true onto one row. Read state is per-browser, so the same notification is unread again on another device. No readAt timestamp.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH the notification's read_at for the signed-in user, server-side, so read state follows the user across devices.
operations.validation: no existence check — an unknown id is a silent no-op

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Maps read: true over the whole (max-50) array. No timestamp, no audit, per-browser.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a bulk mark-read scoped to the signed-in recipient with a server-side cutoff timestamp so rows arriving mid-request are not silently swallowed.

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only, and the thinnest record in the store: the decision is written as a bare map entry `approvals[id] = 'approved'|'modified'|'rejected'` — no decider, no timestamp, no comment, no modified payload (so the 'modified' outcome records nothing about WHAT was modified). The code comment claims 'A decision resumes the paused run'; nothing resumes anything — no run object is touched and no execution exists. The audit row it writes carries the hardcoded actor 'owner'/'Org_admin' from auditEvent(), not the signed-in user, and ip ''. The notification then tells the user 'The decision is recorded in the audit trail with actor and timestamp.'
operations.requiredBehaviour: An approval decision must be a first-class row — approval_id, decided_by (the real session user), decided_at, decision, reason, and the modified payload when decision='modified' — written in the same transaction that resumes or cancels the paused run in the execution service. Human-in-the-loop decisions are the audit evidence for an agent acting; they cannot be a client-side map.
operations.authorization: designated approver for that guardrail/policy — currently anyone; a user can approve their own run
operations.validation: no check that the approval exists, is still pending, or is assigned to this user; no reason required for a rejection
operations.sideEffect: audit row with a fabricated actor + a notification claiming the actor was recorded

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. A public method letting ANY screen append an arbitrary row to the 'append-only' audit trail, then .slice(0, 500) — so the trail is neither append-only nor complete: row 501 deletes the oldest evidence with no archive. Combined with auditEvent()'s hardcoded user/role, the trail is client-authored fiction: a user can write rows attributing actions to 'owner'/'Org_admin' or delete old ones by generating 500 new ones.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Audit rows must be written by the server as a side effect of the action itself, in the same transaction, with the actor from the session, the real client IP, and append-only storage (no client write path, no cap, retention by policy rather than by array length).
operations.apiMethodPath: none — server-side emission only; GET /tenants/{tenantId}/audit for reading
operations.authorization: write: server only. read: org admin / auditor
operations.validation: none — arbitrary action, resource, status and actor accepted
operations.sideEffect: evicts the 501st-oldest audit row

operations.currentBehaviour: FABRICATES IDENTITY. The factory every audited mutation calls defaults user: 'owner', role: 'Org_admin', status: 'Success', ip: '' and — when the caller omits it — resourceId: crypto.randomUUID(), i.e. a random id that points at no record. The type only permits user 'owner' | '', so the trail literally cannot name a real person even though src/lib/auth.tsx has the signed-in user's id and email. Every audit row in the product therefore records the same fake actor, an empty IP, and sometimes a meaningless resource id.
operations.requiredBehaviour: actor_user_id, actor_email, actor_role, ip and user_agent must come from the authenticated request server-side. status must reflect the real outcome (today nothing can ever be 'Failed'). resourceId must always be the real resource's id — never a random uuid.
operations.validation: resourceId falls back to a random uuid instead of failing

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES A RESULT: a brand-new tenant is seeded with three audit rows so the trail is never empty — and two of them are byte-identical 'trial.started' / 'subscription' events, a duplicate that is almost certainly a copy-paste bug now shown to users as real history. All three get random resourceIds from the auditEvent fallback, and 'org.created' is stamped with the current clock rather than the real org creation time.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Audit rows must be emitted by the real events: one row when the tenant is created (at the real timestamp, by the real creator) and one when the trial actually starts. Never seed a trail to make it look populated.
operations.apiMethodPath: n/a — emitted by tenant creation / billing
operations.validation: n/a
operations.sideEffect: shows fabricated, duplicated history on the audit screen

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Appends {...input, id: uuid, status: 'ACTIVE'} — status is forced, never chosen. A legal entity with currency, country and parentId created with no validation of any of them: no ISO-4217 currency check, no ISO-3166 country check, no uniqueness on `code`, and parentId is accepted without verifying the parent exists or that the hierarchy stays acyclic.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with server validation of code uniqueness per tenant, currency/country against ISO lists, and parent existence + cycle prevention on the hierarchy.
operations.validation: none: code uniqueness, currency, country and parent all unchecked
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'company.created'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only, with a branch on the magic string id 'primary': that path writes a sparse Partial<Company> into `primaryOverride` instead of a row, because the primary legal entity is derived from the session org name and has no record. So one method writes to two different shapes depending on a sentinel. Blind patch merge — a caller can flip `status`, reparent the entity, or change its currency after transactions exist, with no checks. Audit row does not record which fields changed.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Make the primary company a real row at tenant creation and delete the sentinel. PATCH with field-level validation, immutability rules for currency once postings exist, cycle checks on parentId, and a before/after diff in the audit row.
operations.validation: no field validation, no cycle check, no immutability rules
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'company.updated' with no diff

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Appends {fromId, toId, eliminationAccount, id: uuid}. fromId/toId hold Company ids OR the sentinel 'primary'; nothing checks that either entity exists, that they differ, or that the pair is not already recorded. eliminationAccount is free text with no chart of accounts behind it. THERE IS NO DELETE OR UPDATE for this record anywhere on the context — a mistyped pair is permanent.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with FK-enforced company ids, a CHECK that from <> to, a unique constraint on the unordered pair, and eliminationAccount as a FK into a real chart of accounts. Add update and delete endpoints.
operations.validation: no existence, self-pair, duplicate or account validation
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'intercompany.paired'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {...policy, id: uuid}. The policy has real semantics on paper — type, action (hitl/redact/block/warn), checkPoint (Input/Output/Both), scope — but NOTHING evaluates guardrails at runtime, so creating one changes no behaviour; it only adds a row to a list. `scope` is 'Global' or an app code as a loose string with no FK to installed apps.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a policy the agent runtime actually loads and enforces at the named checkpoint, with scope as a validated reference to Global or an installed app, and a test/preview path so an admin can see what a policy would block.
operations.validation: scope not validated against installed apps; no duplicate-name check
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'policy.created'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Blind Partial merge, including `active` — so the five seeded policies (PII redaction, spend cap, rate limit...) can be switched off from the browser with no approval, no reason and no diff in the audit row. Unknown id is a silent no-op that still writes a 'policy.updated' audit row claiming success.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH with a before/after diff in the audit row, a required reason when deactivating a policy, and a 404 (not a silent success) for an unknown id. Deactivating a compliance-relevant policy should require elevated rights.
operations.authorization: security admin; deactivation should be separately privileged
operations.validation: no existence check, no diff, no reason
operations.sideEffect: audit row that says Success even when nothing matched

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter — the policy is gone with no soft-delete, no confirmation and no record of what it contained. The seeded policies are referenced BY NAME elsewhere in the app (the approval queue names two of them, the sample trace names a third), so deleting one leaves those screens pointing at a policy that no longer exists.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Soft-delete (deleted_at + deleted_by) so historical runs and approvals can still explain which policy fired, with a referential check before removal.
operations.validation: no confirmation, no reference check
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'policy.deleted' that does not preserve the deleted policy

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES A RESULT: browser localStorage only. Mints a credential IN THE BROWSER — `apr_rnr_` + a uuid with dashes stripped, truncated to 24 chars — and stores it in plaintext in localStorage, in a field the type comments call 'a one-time secret'. It is registered with nothing, so no runner can ever authenticate with it; status is 'pending' forever because there is no server for an agent to call home to. pairedAt is stamped at creation even though nothing paired.
operations.requiredBehaviour: The server issues the pairing token, returns it exactly once for display, stores only a hash, gives it a short expiry and single use, and flips the runner to 'online' on first authenticated heartbeat. Add rotation and revocation. A browser must never mint a credential.
operations.authorization: org admin — credential issuance must be privileged
operations.validation: no name uniqueness; token has no expiry, no scope, no revocation
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'runner.paired' for a pairing that did not happen; plaintext secret persisted to disk

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Array filter. Because the token was never registered, nothing is revoked — if a real runner ever existed it would keep working after being 'removed'.
operations.requiredBehaviour: DELETE must revoke the runner's credential server-side and terminate its sessions, then soft-delete the row for audit.
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'runner.removed' with no actual revocation

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Stores {connectorId, name, account, secretHint, createdAt}. To its credit the shape stores only a hint, not the secret — but there is nowhere for the real secret to go, so the connection is decorative: nothing can authenticate to the external system. connectorId is a loose string with no FK to the connector catalogue, and no connectivity test is ever run.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST the credential to the server, store it in a secrets manager or encrypted column (never the browser), persist only the metadata plus a hint, run a live connectivity test before marking the connection usable, and record last_verified_at.
operations.validation: connectorId unvalidated; no connectivity test; no duplicate-account check
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'connection.created'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Array filter; no revocation of any OAuth grant or API key (there is none to revoke), and retentionPolicies rows pointing at this connectorId are left dangling.
operations.requiredBehaviour: DELETE must revoke the stored credential at the provider where possible, purge the secret, and either cascade or block when retention policies or syncs reference it.
operations.validation: no dependency check against retentionPolicies
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'connection.removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Records {name, baseUrl, auth, operations: number, source: 'manual'|'openapi'}. `operations` is a COUNT the caller supplies — the actual operations are never stored, so an 'openapi' import keeps a number and throws the spec away. baseUrl is unvalidated (no scheme check, no SSRF guard), and `auth` is a bare string describing a scheme with no credential anywhere.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST should persist the parsed OpenAPI document and a child operations table (method, path, params, auth), validate and allow-list baseUrl against SSRF, and store credentials in the secrets manager.
operations.validation: no URL validation, no SSRF guard, operations is a self-reported integer
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'connector.registered'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Array filter; connections and retention policies referencing it are not checked.
operations.requiredBehaviour: DELETE with a referential check against connections and retention policies, plus soft-delete for audit.
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'connector.removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Replaces the whole array of tab names that external partner users may see. This is ACCESS CONTROL stored as a list of display strings in the tenant admin's own browser — a client portal user's browser has its own localStorage and would never see this value at all. Tab names are unvalidated free text.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Portal visibility must be enforced server-side on every portal request, keyed by a stable tab id rather than a label, and evaluated against the portal user's role — never read from the admin's browser.
operations.validation: no validation that a name is a real tab
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'portal.tabs_updated' with resourceId hardcoded to the literal 'tabs'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Appends a role carrying permissions: Record<string, {read, comment, download, hidden[]}> and, when isDefault is set, clears isDefault on every other role in the same pass — a uniqueness rule enforced by a map() instead of a partial unique index, so a concurrent write from another tab can leave two defaults. Again: an authorization model living in one admin's browser, enforcing nothing.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a role row with a partial unique index on (tenant_id) WHERE is_default, permissions normalised into rows rather than a nested blob, and every portal request authorised server-side against it.
operations.validation: no name uniqueness; default-role uniqueness enforced only client-side
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'portal.role_created'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter with NO check that the role is assigned to portal users and NO check that it is the default — deleting the default role leaves the tenant with no default and no warning.
operations.requiredBehaviour: DELETE must refuse while users are assigned (or require an explicit reassignment target) and must refuse to remove the default role unless another is promoted in the same transaction.
operations.validation: no assignment check, no default-role guard
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'portal.role_removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Appends with a DERIVED COMPOSITE ID `${field.entity}.${field.field}` — so re-adding the same entity/field pair creates a genuine duplicate primary key inside the array, and every downstream update/remove by id then hits whichever copy map/filter reaches first. This is the GDPR Art. 30 record of processing: legalBasis and retention are unvalidated free text ('Consent', 'Per KYC policy'), and the register seeds itself with 16 hardcoded platform rows, so a tenant's register describes the platform's tables rather than the tenant's own data.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with a unique constraint on (tenant_id, entity, field), legalBasis constrained to the six GDPR Art. 6 bases, retention as a structured duration plus a policy reference, and the seeded catalogue clearly separated from tenant-authored rows.
operations.validation: no uniqueness on the derived id; legalBasis and retention unconstrained
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'inventory.field_added' whose resourceId is the field NAME, not the id

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Blind Partial merge by id. Patching `entity` or `field` does NOT recompute the derived `${entity}.${field}` id, so the row's id immediately stops matching its own contents. No diff recorded, no reviewer, no version history on a compliance register.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH with the identity columns immutable (or the key recomputed transactionally), a full change history on the register, and an approver recorded for changes to legal basis or retention.
operations.validation: id/content divergence on rename; no diff
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'inventory.field_updated'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter removes a row from the record of processing with no soft-delete and no reason — a compliance register that can be silently shortened, including the six rows flagged `sensitive`.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Soft-delete only, with reason and approver, and full history retained: a processing register must be reconstructible as at any past date.
operations.validation: no reason, no approval, no retention of the removed row
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'inventory.field_removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Appends {...flow, id: uuid} — note the SEEDED rows use slug ids ('ai-inference') while created rows use uuids, so the same column holds two id schemes. `crossBorder` is free text ('SCC + DPA', or '') standing in for a transfer-mechanism decision; source and destination are display strings, not references to connectors or systems. There is NO update and NO delete for data flows on the context.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with one id scheme, source/destination as FKs to systems or connectors, and crossBorder as a constrained transfer-mechanism reference. Add update and delete endpoints — a mapped flow is currently permanent.
operations.validation: none; no duplicate-name check despite the audit row keying on the name
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'flow.mapped' whose resourceId is the flow NAME

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {title, activity, risk: Low|Medium|High, status: Draft|In review|Approved, id: uuid}. A Data Protection Impact Assessment reduced to four fields with NO assessor, NO date, NO mitigations, NO reviewer, NO attached document — and status 'Approved' is settable directly at creation by whoever fills the form. There is no update and no delete method, so a DPIA can never be revised or withdrawn.
operations.requiredBehaviour: A DPIA needs author, created/updated dates, the processing activities it covers as references, identified risks and mitigations, a reviewer with a sign-off timestamp, and a state machine where 'Approved' can only be reached through review. Add update/withdraw endpoints.
operations.authorization: DPO; approval must be a separate privileged transition
operations.validation: no state machine — 'Approved' can be set on creation; no required mitigations
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'dpia.created' whose resourceId is the TITLE

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {name, profiling: boolean, humanReview: boolean, status: 'Registered'|'Needs review', id: uuid}. The register of automated decision-making is four fields with no link to the agent, artifact or policy that does the deciding, no description of the logic, no safeguards field, and no date. status is caller-supplied. No update, no delete.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Link each entry to the actual agent/artifact, record the decision logic description, the safeguards offered to data subjects, the reviewer and review date, and derive status from review state rather than accepting it from the form.
operations.validation: no link to the deciding system; status caller-supplied
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'decision.registered' whose resourceId is the NAME

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only, and inert: the row says data pulled through a connector is kept keepForDays then purged, but NOTHING PURGES ANYTHING — there is no job, and `lastRun` is a string the creator supplies rather than a timestamp any run wrote. connectorId is an unvalidated string with no FK, `enabled` is decorative, and nothing prevents two policies for the same connector.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a policy a real scheduled purge job consumes, with connectorId as a FK, a unique constraint per connector, keepForDays validated against the legal minimum for that data class, and last_run_at written only by the job itself alongside a purge receipt.
operations.validation: connectorId unvalidated; no per-connector uniqueness; keepForDays unbounded; lastRun user-supplied
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'retention.policy_set' whose resourceId is the connectorId

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter — a retention rule disappears with no record of what it required or who removed it.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Soft-delete with reason and actor; retention decisions must remain reconstructible.
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'retention.policy_removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {...report, id: uuid, createdAt: now}. A `total` is accepted as a single number from the caller — THERE ARE NO EXPENSE LINE ITEMS ANYWHERE IN THE STORE, so the report has an amount with nothing behind it, no receipts, no categories, no claimant and no company/cost-centre. `currency` is a free string and the total carries no exchange rate. teSettings.receiptRequiredAbove, categoryLimits and flagDuplicates are never consulted here.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a report with an expense_lines child table (date, category, merchant, amount, currency, receipt attachment, tax fields), the total computed server-side from the lines, a claimant from the session, a company/cost-centre reference, and the tenant's own T&E policy checks applied at submit.
operations.authorization: claimant self-service; the claimant must be recorded, not implied
operations.validation: total unvalidated and uncorroborated; currency unvalidated; no line items; policy settings ignored
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'expense.report_created'

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES A WORKFLOW: browser localStorage only. Walks a hard-coded array ['Draft','Submitted','Approved','Reimbursed'] one index forward and clamps at the end. There is no approver — 'Approved' is reached by the same person pressing the same button again, with nobody recorded as having approved it and no comment. teSettings.approvalLevels (Reporting manager, Finance > 1000) is completely ignored by this function. Reaching 'Reimbursed' here stamps reimbursedAt and claims the money is paid with no payment run involved at all.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Replace with explicit, separately authorised transitions (submit / approve / reject / recall), each recording the actor, timestamp and comment, each validated against the tenant's configured approval levels and thresholds, with rejection and send-back paths that this one-way ratchet does not have. 'Reimbursed' must only ever be set by a real disbursement.
operations.authorization: submit: claimant. approve: the configured approver for the amount — currently anyone, including the claimant approving their own claim
operations.validation: no approver check, no threshold check, no rejection path, no reason
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'expense.report_advanced' that does not say from what, to what, or by whom

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts with status forced to 'Active'. The status union is only 'Active' | 'Closed' — there is NO pending/approved/rejected state, so a travel request is approved by existing. start/end are unvalidated strings (no ordering check), estimatedCost has no currency, and `project` and `budgetHead` are display strings, not references. teSettings.travel (advancePercent 80, approvalAbove, perDiem) and travelNotifications are not consulted; no advance is created and no notification is sent.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with a real request lifecycle (Draft/Submitted/Approved/Rejected/Closed), date validation, currency on the estimate, project and budget head as FKs, and the configured approval threshold and advance policy applied by the server.
operations.validation: no date ordering, no currency, no approval state, settings ignored
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'travel.request_created'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Flips status to 'Closed'. No closedAt, no closer, no settlement: a request with an advance is closed without reconciling it against actual expenses, because there are no advances and no link from a travel request to any expense report.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a close that settles the advance against the claimed expenses, records closed_at and closed_by, and refuses to close while linked expense reports are unsettled.
operations.validation: no settlement check, no timestamp, no actor
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'travel.request_closed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Appends parsed rows, de-duplicating on the composite key `${date}|${merchant}|${amount}` against rows already stored — which means two genuinely identical same-day charges at the same merchant for the same amount are silently DISCARDED as duplicates, and a re-import of an amended statement cannot correct an earlier row. No card/account identifier on the row at all, no currency, no import batch record, no statement reference, no employee.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Import against a card_statement_imports batch row (file, account, period, imported_by), match on the issuer's own transaction id where available rather than a lossy composite, keep rejected/duplicate rows visible for review instead of dropping them, and carry card account, currency and cardholder on every transaction.
operations.validation: no card account, no currency, no amount/date parsing guarantees, silent drops
operations.sideEffect: audit row whose resourceId is the literal string '<n> rows' rather than any id

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES A RESULT AND MISCOUNTS: browser localStorage only. Matches an unmatched charge to the FIRST expense report whose total is within half a cent of the charge amount — amount equality alone: no date window, no merchant, no claimant, no currency check, and the same report can be matched by several different charges because nothing marks a report as consumed. It returns a count accumulated in a closure variable mutated INSIDE the setState updater, so under React StrictMode (dev) the updater runs twice and the number reported to the user is double the real one. The UI then shows that number as 'matched'.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Matching must run server-side against expense LINES (not report totals) using amount + date window + merchant + claimant, must be one-to-one, must record a confidence and leave ambiguous candidates for human confirmation, and must return the count from the persisted result rather than a closure counter.
operations.validation: amount-only matching against report totals; no one-to-one guarantee; no currency check
operations.sideEffect: returns a count that is doubled in React StrictMode; writes NO audit row despite mutating financial matching data

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Sums the totals of the selected reports (mixing currencies blindly — ExpenseReport.currency is per-report and never checked) into one `total`, stores reportIds as a bare string ARRAY inside the row, and starts the run at stage 'Request Processed'. No payment method, no bank account, no payment file, no approver, no run reference number. Nothing stops the same report being included in two runs, or a Draft report being paid.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a payment batch with a child reimbursement_run_items table (FK to the report, amount, currency), single-currency or FX-explicit totals, a check that every report is Approved and not already in an open run, a human-readable run reference, and the payment instrument recorded.
operations.validation: no status check on the reports, no double-inclusion check, no currency check, reportIds not a FK
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'reimbursement.run_created'

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES MONEY MOVING: browser localStorage only. Steps a hard-coded stage array ['Request Processed','Moved to Accounts','Batch Generation','Disbursed'] one index forward. When the next stage is 'Disbursed' it ALSO flips every ExpenseReport named in the run to status 'Reimbursed' with reimbursedAt = now — the comment says 'Disbursing a run is what actually reimburses the reports inside it'. No payment provider, no bank file, no ledger posting, no payment reference, no failure path, no partial disbursement, and no approval before disbursing. If the run id is unknown, nextStage is computed as '' and the map writes an EMPTY STRING into stage, corrupting the row silently.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Disbursement must be an integration with a real payment rail: generate the payment instruction, record provider reference, per-item success/failure, and mark reports reimbursed ONLY on a confirmed settlement callback. Every stage transition needs an actor, a timestamp and an authorisation step; an unknown id must 404 rather than blank the stage. The provider contract itself is unknown from this codebase and must be specified before implementation.
operations.apiMethodPath: POST /tenants/{tenantId}/reimbursement-runs/{id}/advance (and a provider webhook for settlement)
operations.authorization: payments role with separation of duties from the approver — currently anyone
operations.validation: unknown id writes stage = ''; no approval gate before Disbursed; no reversal path
operations.sideEffect: silently marks arbitrary expense reports as paid

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Shallow spread of a Partial over the settings object, so passing a nested key (travel, receiptEmail, categoryLimits, approvalLevels...) REPLACES that whole sub-object rather than merging it — a caller patching one travel field wipes the other two. None of these settings are enforced by any other method in the store: enforcement 'warn'|'block', receiptRequiredAbove, flagDuplicates, categoryLimits, approvalLevels and slaDays are read by nothing. The audit row is a generic 'travel_expense.settings_updated' on resourceId 'TE' with no indication of what changed.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH individual settings with per-field validation (thresholds as numeric + currency, slaDays bounded, approval levels ordered and non-overlapping), a change history with before/after and actor, and — crucially — enforcement of those settings in the submit/approve paths.
operations.validation: shallow merge clobbers nested objects; thresholds are strings; nothing enforces the settings
operations.sideEffect: audit row with no diff

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Mints the customer-facing reference as `SUP-${String(prev.tickets.length + 1).padStart(4,'0')}` — AN INCREMENTED ARRAY-LENGTH COUNTER, not a sequence: delete a ticket and the next one reuses a live reference; two tabs create SUP-0002 twice. slaBreached is hard-coded false and csat null at creation, and NOTHING EVER SETS slaBreached — no SLA clock exists, despite supportSettings.csat.slaWarnPercent and tierPolicies implying one. `requester` and `assignee` are display-name strings, not user/contact ids. status, priority, category and source are free strings not validated against the configured FieldRow lists.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with the reference from a per-tenant Postgres sequence, requester as a FK to a contact, assignee as a FK to a user, status/priority/category/source validated against the tenant's configured option lists, and SLA target computed from the tier policy at creation with a real job flagging breaches.
operations.authorization: agent, or the requester via the portal/widget
operations.validation: reference collides; no FKs; no option-list validation; SLA never evaluated
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'support.ticket_created' whose resourceId is the reference

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Blind Partial merge over the whole ticket, with one piece of real logic: if patch.status is 'Resolved' or 'Closed' it sets resolvedAt (keeping any earlier value). Everything else is unguarded — the reference, createdAt, csat and slaBreached can all be overwritten by a caller; reopening a ticket does NOT clear resolvedAt, so a reopened ticket keeps a resolution time and any resolution metric silently lies. No ticket comments, replies or conversation exist anywhere in the store, so 'updating' a ticket can never mean answering the customer. No status-transition rules, no assignment notification, no CSAT survey despite csat.sendOnResolve being configured.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH with immutable identity columns, a validated status transition graph, resolvedAt cleared on reopen, a ticket_events/replies child table for the actual conversation, assignment notifications, and the configured CSAT survey genuinely dispatched on resolve.
operations.validation: no immutability, no transition rules, reopen leaves a stale resolvedAt
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'support.ticket_updated' with no diff

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {...article, id: uuid, updatedAt: now}. state is 'draft'|'published'|'archived' supplied by the caller — an article can be created directly as 'published' with no review. `category` is a display-name STRING matched against the kbCategories string array, not an id. No author, no createdAt (only updatedAt), no slug, no version history; body is unsanitised free text.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with author and created_at, category as a FK, a slug, a publish transition separate from creation, body sanitised on render, and article versions retained.
operations.validation: category is a loose string; no slug; no review gate before 'published'
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'support.article_created' whose resourceId is the TITLE

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter, no soft-delete, no check whether the article is referenced by supportSettings.indexedArticles (a parallel string array that is not cleaned up here, leaving a dangling entry).
operations.requiredBehaviour: Soft-delete (or archive), cascade the search index entry, and keep the body for restore.
operations.validation: leaves indexedArticles dangling
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'support.article_removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Pushes a raw display string onto an array if not already present — the dedupe is case- and whitespace-sensitive, so 'Billing' and 'billing ' both live. NO AUDIT ROW (one of the few mutations with none), no id, no delete method, no rename. Articles then point at these by name, so a category can never be renamed without orphaning articles.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a kb_categories row with an id and a normalised unique name per tenant; articles reference the id. Add rename and delete with a reassignment path.
operations.validation: case/whitespace-sensitive dedupe; no length limit
operations.sideEffect: none — no audit row is written

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {title, body, id: uuid}. No shortcut/keyword, no owner, no category, no variables, no createdAt — and no update method, so a typo can only be fixed by delete-and-recreate.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with a shortcut key, owner/visibility scope, created/updated timestamps and a defined placeholder syntax. Add an update endpoint.
operations.validation: no title uniqueness
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'support.canned_created' whose resourceId is the TITLE

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Soft-delete so historical replies can still show which template was used.
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'support.canned_removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. One shallow-spread setter for the ENTIRE Support configuration: option lists (statuses/categories/priorities/types/channels), the embedded chat widget, CSAT, and seven separate rule collections (escalationRules, inboxAccounts, inboundChannels, businessHours, autoResponses, shiftHandoffs, reportSchedules) plus tierPolicies and indexedArticles. Any nested key passed replaces its whole sub-object. None of it is enforced or executed: no escalation fires, no inbox is polled, no auto-response is sent, no scheduled report is delivered, no business-hours clock runs, and the widget is never served to any external site. Every edit writes the same opaque audit row on resourceId 'SUP'.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Split into separate resources with their own endpoints and validation (option lists, widget config, CSAT config, and each rule type as its own table), and make each one actually drive the runtime that claims to use it. Record per-setting change history with actor and diff.
operations.validation: shallow merge clobbers nested config; no validation on any rule; nothing enforced
operations.sideEffect: audit row with no diff

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Generates the asset tag as `${type.tagPrefix ?? 'AST-'}${String(seq).padStart(4,'0')}` where seq = COUNT OF EXISTING ASSETS OF THAT TYPE + 1 — an incremented counter, so deleting an asset makes the next one reuse a live tag number, and the fallback 'AST-' silently applies when the type has no taxonomy entry. acquiredAt is set to NOW, which is the creation time, not the acquisition date — a back-dated asset is impossible to record correctly. assignedTo is a display-name string, `project` and `purchase` are strings, warrantyEnd is an unvalidated string. No cost, no supplier, no serial number, no depreciation fields at all.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with the tag from a per-type Postgres sequence, a real acquisition date supplied by the user, assignedTo as a FK to an employee, supplier/cost/serial/invoice captured, warrantyEnd as a date, and depreciation handled by an explicit schedule (the method for which is not specified anywhere in this codebase).
operations.validation: tag collides after deletion; acquiredAt is not the acquisition date; no serial/cost/supplier; assignedTo not a FK
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'asset.created' whose resourceId is the tagNo

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Blind Partial merge — tagNo, type and acquiredAt are all overwritable, and changing `type` does not re-issue the tag, so the tag prefix stops matching the asset type. This is also the only way assignment happens: assigning an asset to a person is a silent field patch with no assignment record, no acceptance, no handover date and no history of who held it before.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH with tagNo and acquiredAt immutable, plus a separate asset_assignments table (asset, holder, from, to, acknowledged_at) so custody history exists. Lifecycle stage changes should be explicit transitions.
operations.validation: no immutability; no custody history; stage is a free string
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'asset.updated' with no diff

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter deletes the asset outright — there is no retirement/disposal path despite the taxonomy shipping 'retirement_reasons', so an asset leaves the register with no reason, no disposal date, no proceeds and no residual value, and its tag number is immediately recyclable by addAsset.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Retirement, not deletion: a disposal transition with reason (from the taxonomy), date, proceeds and approver, keeping the row and its tag permanently reserved.
operations.validation: no reason, no disposal record, tag recycled
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'asset.removed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Reference is `REQ-${String(prev.assetRequests.length + 1).padStart(4,'0')}` — the same array-length counter, same collision. approvedBy is set null, status is caller-supplied free text (so a request can be created already 'Approved'), raisedBy is a display-name string rather than the session user, and assetSettings.approvalLevels — whose only entry names an approver as the literal string 'Manager (unknown)' — is never consulted.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with the reference from a sequence, raisedBy taken from the session as a FK, status forced to the initial state, and the approval chain resolved from the configured levels.
operations.authorization: any employee for self; raiser must be the session user
operations.validation: reference collides; status caller-supplied; raisedBy unverified
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'asset.request_raised' whose resourceId is the reference

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Sets status and approvedBy from two arguments the CALLER supplies — the approver is whatever display-name string the UI passes in, not the signed-in user, so a request can be approved 'by' anyone. status is an unconstrained string, so any value at all is storable. No decidedAt, no comment, no rejection reason, no check against the configured approval levels, and nothing stops the raiser approving their own request. The audit action is built by lower-casing that free-text status (`asset.request_${status.toLowerCase()}`), so a typo creates a brand-new audit action name.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST approve/reject with the decider from the session, a decided_at timestamp, a required reason on rejection, validation against the configured approval level for that request, and a self-approval block.
operations.authorization: the configured approver — currently any caller, naming any approver
operations.validation: approver is caller-supplied; status unconstrained; no self-approval guard; audit action derived from free text
operations.sideEffect: audit row with a caller-influenced action name

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Shallow spread, so patching `taxonomies` replaces ALL NINE taxonomy lists at once and patching `agents` replaces the whole agent-control object. The agent controls (pauseAll, autoRunOnNew, autoPauseAt, disabled[]) govern nothing — no agent runs. Generic audit row on resourceId 'ITAM' with no diff.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Separate endpoints per section (approval levels, custom fields, each taxonomy, agent controls) with per-row validation and a change history carrying actor and diff.
operations.validation: shallow merge clobbers whole sections; taxonomy entries unvalidated
operations.sideEffect: audit row with no diff

operations.currentBehaviour: DESTRUCTIVE AND UNDOABLE: browser localStorage only. Assigns `empty.assetSettings` — the module-level default OBJECT ITSELF, not a copy — wiping every custom field, every taxonomy edit and every approval level with no confirmation, no backup and no restore. Because it is the same object reference shared with `empty`, any later in-place mutation of the tenant's settings would also corrupt the module default for the rest of the session. The comment claims it restores 'the platform default its Change History names', but ITAM has no change history in this store (only POS does).
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a reset that snapshots the current settings first, requires explicit confirmation, records actor and timestamp, and writes a restorable change-history entry. Never hand out a shared reference to a module-level default.
operations.validation: no confirmation, no snapshot, shared object reference

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {...rfp, id: uuid, createdAt: now}. `stage` is free text with no state machine ('Your turn', 'Drafting', 'Out for client', 'Extracting' appear in the sample), `estimate` is a number with no currency, `vertical` and `schema` are display-name strings — `schema` in particular is supposed to point at a CustomSchema but stores its NAME. deadline is an unvalidated string, often ''. No owner, no source document, no attachments.

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Blind Partial merge including createdAt and stage; no transition rules and no updatedAt field exists on the type, so an RFP never records when it last moved. operations.authorization: the RFP's owner or sales admin

operations.sideEffect: audit row 'pitch.rfp_updated'

No confirmation, no audit row, no undo.

No address, no phone, no currency, no payment terms, no credit limit, no customer-group link even though posSettings.customerGroups exists.

Tax-identifier FORMAT rules are jurisdiction-specific and are not defined anywhere in this codebase — they must be specified, not guessed.

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only, and the single most consequential fake in the store. ONE method creates all nine order-to-cash document kinds — quotation, order, delivery, invoice, return, credit, refund, contract, subscription — into ONE flat array, with the reference minted as `${prefix}-${String(count of that kind + 1).padStart(4,'0')}` (QT/SO/DN/INV/RMA/CN/RF/RC/SUB). That is an incremented array counter: DELETE AN INVOICE AND THE NEXT INVOICE REUSES ITS NUMBER, and two tabs mint the same number. THERE ARE NO LINE ITEMS — `total` is a single caller-supplied number with no currency, no tax breakdown and nothing behind it; matchSettings and posSettings.taxCategories are never consulted. `customer` stores the customer's NAME, not the PosCustomer id. There is no link between a quotation and the order it became, or an invoice and its delivery — the three-way match the app advertises has nothing to match on.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Separate tables per document kind (or one header table with a kind discriminator) plus a line-items child table; references from per-tenant per-kind Postgres sequences that are gap-free and never reused; customer_id as a FK; currency on every document; predecessor/successor document links so quotation→order→delivery→invoice is traceable; totals computed from lines server-side. Invoice numbering and tax treatment are statutory in most jurisdictions — the applicable rules are NOT defined in this codebase and must be specified before implementation.
operations.authorization: sales user; issuing an invoice or credit note should be separately privileged
operations.validation: reference collides and is reusable; no line items; no currency; no tax; customer is a name; no document chaining; status is a free string
operations.sideEffect: audit row `pos.<kind>_created` whose resourceId is the reference

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Blind Partial merge over any field of any document kind — including `reference`, `total`, `kind` and `createdAt`. An issued invoice's amount or number can be silently rewritten after the fact, with the audit row saying only 'pos.doc_updated' and no diff.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Issued financial documents must be immutable: corrections happen via credit notes or amendments, not field patches. PATCH should be limited to non-financial fields on unissued drafts, with a full field-level change history.
operations.authorization: sales user for drafts only; issued documents locked
operations.validation: nothing immutable; no status transition rules
operations.sideEffect: audit row with no diff

operations.currentBehaviour: DESTRUCTIVE: browser localStorage only. Hard filter deletes an INVOICE (or credit note, or refund) outright, with NO AUDIT ROW AT ALL — the one deletion in the financial area that leaves no trace — and it frees that document's number for reuse by the next addPosDoc of the same kind.

operations.validation: no draft-only guard, no reason, number recycled
operations.sideEffect: none — no audit row is written for deleting a financial document

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {cashier, openingFloat, currency, warehouse, notes, openedAt: now, cashTaken: 0, cardTaken: 0, id}. cashTaken and cardTaken are initialised to 0 AND NOTHING EVER INCREMENTS THEM — no sale posts to a shift anywhere in the store, so the variance maths at close is always computed against zero takings. `cashier` and `warehouse` are display-name strings, not FKs. Nothing prevents the same cashier or till having two shifts open at once.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST with cashier_id and till/warehouse as FKs, a partial unique index preventing a second open shift per till, and takings accumulated server-side from actual posted sales.
operations.validation: no single-open-shift rule; cashier/warehouse are strings; takings never accrue
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'pos.shift_opened' whose resourceId is the CASHIER NAME

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Stamps closedAt and stores countedCash. Because cashTaken is permanently 0, the cash variance every downstream screen computes is meaningless, and the configured thresholds (posSettings.cashVariance: reasonAbove 1, redWorst 5...) are never applied here — no reason is demanded for a variance, and no approval is required. A shift can be closed twice (no guard on closedAt already being set), overwriting the first close.
operations.requiredBehaviour: POST a close that computes expected cash from the shift's actual posted sales, requires a reason when the variance exceeds the configured threshold, blocks re-closing, and records who counted and who approved the variance.
operations.authorization: cashier to count, supervisor to approve a variance
operations.validation: no re-close guard, no variance reason, thresholds ignored
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'pos.shift_closed'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Flat Partial merge over the three-way-match tolerances. priceAction and quantityAction store PROSE as enum values ('Warn — flag it, allow the post'), which no code can safely branch on and which breaks the moment the wording changes. Nothing enforces any of it: there is no matching engine, and the POS documents have no line items to match. Note this setter does NOT write a PosChange history entry, unlike updatePosSettings — so match-tolerance edits are invisible in the app's own Change History.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH with actions as stable enum codes (warn|block|allow) rendered as labels in the UI, tolerances validated as non-negative numbers with an explicit percent-vs-absolute unit, a change-history entry like every other POS setting, and a matching engine that actually applies them.
operations.validation: prose as enum; no unit on tolerances; no change-history entry
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'pos.match_settings_updated' on resourceId 'POS'

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Shallow spread of the patch, then unshifts a PosChange {id, at: now, by: 'owner', summary, reverted: false} — `by` is the HARDCODED LITERAL 'owner', so the app's own Change History attributes every change to a fake actor, and the `summary` is whatever prose the calling screen passed, not a computed diff, so it can describe a change that did not happen. `reverted` is written false and NOTHING EVER SETS IT TRUE — there is no revert method on the context, so the field that makes a change 'undoable' is decorative. Patching a nested section (taxCategories, loyalty, cashVariance, agents) replaces it wholesale.
operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH per section with the actor from the session, a server-computed before/after diff rather than a caller-supplied sentence, and a real revert endpoint that restores the recorded previous value and flips reverted.
operations.validation: summary is caller-supplied prose; actor hardcoded; shallow merge clobbers sections; revert unimplemented
operations.sideEffect: writes a Change History entry with a fabricated author

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only, and deliberately schemaless: every create dialog in CRM and HR that has no bespoke model writes here as {id, createdAt, title, fields: Record<string,string>} under an untyped surface key like 'crm.leads' or 'hr.employees'. EVERY VALUE IS A STRING — a salary, a date of birth, a deal value and a phone number are all stored as text with no type, no validation, no required fields and no relationships. The key is also interpolated straight into the audit action (`${key}.created`), so the audit vocabulary is whatever string a screen passes. This is the store's admission that whole domains have no data model: the comment at line 145 says these surfaces exist 'rather than being inert'.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Each surface needs a real typed table with real columns, FKs and validation — a lead is not a bag of strings. Until those exist, an untyped record must at minimum carry its schema id, typed values, created_by and a constrained audit action. Nothing about these records can be migrated to a production schema without first defining what each surface actually is.
operations.validation: no schema, no types, no required fields, no relationships, audit action caller-controlled
operations.sideEffect: audit row `<key>.created` whose resourceId is the TITLE

operations.currentBehaviour: browser localStorage only. Hard filter within the keyed bucket, no confirmation, no soft-delete, and the audit action is again built from the caller's key (`${key}.deleted`). Deleting the last record leaves an empty array under the key rather than removing it.
operations.requiredBehaviour: Per-surface DELETE with soft-delete, confirmation and a constrained audit action.
operations.validation: no confirmation; caller-controlled audit action
operations.sideEffect: audit row `<key>.deleted`

operations.currentBehaviour: FAKES A CAPABILITY: browser localStorage only. Unshifts {...schedule, id: uuid}. There is no scheduler anywhere in this codebase — nothing reads this list and nothing ever fires. `cadence` is free-text prose that no cron parser could accept, `nextRun` is a string set once at creation and never recomputed (so it goes stale immediately and permanently), and `target` names the agent/pipeline by DISPLAY NAME rather than id. `active` defaults to whatever the caller passes.

operations.validation: cadence unparseable; nextRun never recomputed; target is a name; no timezone
operations.sideEffect: audit row 'schedule.created'

operations.sideEffect: audit row 'schedule.removed'

operations.requiredBehaviour: PATCH active with an audit row, next_run_at recomputed from the cadence on resume, and the runner informed.
operations.validation: no audit row; nextRun not recomputed
operations.sideEffect: none — no audit row

Two of the five tasks read real state (artifacts.length > 0, installed.length > 0) but 'Install an enterprise app' IS TRUE ON A BRAND-NEW TENANT because defaultInstalled seeds CRM and HR at line 729 — the task is pre-ticked before the user has done anything. The other three read the localStorage booleans set by setFlag, so 'Allocate credits to yourself', 'Invite a teammate' and 'Try the AI Copilot' are ticked by a flag rather than by the thing happening. checklistDone (line 2234) counts these and drives the onboarding progress number.

openQuestions: TENANCY: the store has no tenant_id and no user_id anywhere, yet src/lib/auth.tsx already exposes activeTenantId, tenants[] and switchTenant. Which of these records are tenant-scoped, which are user-scoped (dismissedChecklist, notification read state, and twoFactor are clearly per-user today but sit in tenant state), and what must happen to loaded state when switchTenant fires?

CREDITS: MONTHLY_CREDITS is a hardcoded 1000 and creditsUsed only ever increases. What is the real credit model — per tenant or per user, what resets it and on what cycle, what happens at zero (hard block or overage), and how do plan tiers change it? Nothing in the code answers this.

TRIAL: TRIAL_DAYS = 13 is a constant with no start date, and the seeded audit trail claims a trial started at page-load time. Where does the trial period actually come from, and what happens when it expires?
APP QUOTA: APP_QUOTA = 5 is exposed as appQuota but install() never checks it. Is it a hard limit, a plan-tier limit, or advisory?

REIMBURSEMENT DISBURSAL: advanceReimbursementRun marks expense reports paid when a stage string reaches 'Disbursed'. No payment provider, bank-file format, settlement callback or reversal path is defined anywhere in this codebase. The payment rail and its contract must be specified before this can be implemented — do not infer one.

EXPENSE / TRAVEL POLICY: teSettings carries enforcement warn|block, receiptRequiredAbove, categoryLimits, approvalLevels (thresholds as bare strings with no currency), slaDays 21, travel.advancePercent 80 and perDiem — none of which any code reads. Which of these are company policy, which are statutory, what currency are the thresholds in, and how is per-diem computed? Not inferable, and must not be invented.

EXPENSE LINE ITEMS: ExpenseReport has a single `total` and there are no expense lines, receipts, categories or tax fields anywhere in the store. What does a line item look like, and what tax treatment applies?

POS INVOICE NUMBERING AND TAX: references come from an array counter and PosDoc has no line items, no currency and no tax breakdown, while posSettings.taxCategories carries withinState/interState fields that nothing uses. Invoice numbering rules, tax categories and their application are jurisdiction-specific statutory matters that are not defined in this repository — they must be specified, not guessed.
POS CUSTOMER taxId: stored as an unvalidated free string with no jurisdiction. What identifier is it and what format rules apply?

DOCUMENT CHAINING: quotation → order → delivery → invoice → return/credit/refund all live in one flat array with no predecessor links, and matchSettings describes a three-way match with nothing to match on. What is the intended document flow and what must the match compare?

ASSET DEPRECIATION AND DISPOSAL: Asset has no cost, supplier, serial number, residual value or depreciation method, and removeAsset hard-deletes instead of retiring despite a 'retirement_reasons' taxonomy. What depreciation policy applies, and what must a disposal record capture?

ASSET APPROVALS: assetSettings.approvalLevels ships one level whose approver is the literal string 'Manager (unknown)', and decideAssetRequest ignores it entirely while letting the caller name the approver. How are approvers actually resolved — by role, by reporting line, or by named user?

SUPPORT SLA: Ticket.slaBreached is written false at creation and never set by anything; supportSettings carries slaWarnPercent, tierPolicies (tier → SLA policy name) and businessHours rules that nothing evaluates. What are the SLA targets per tier/priority, and are they measured against business hours?

TICKET CONVERSATION: there are no ticket replies, comments or events anywhere in the store. What is the conversation model, and which channels (the inboxAccounts / inboundChannels rules are empty shells) must be ingested?

COMPLIANCE REGISTERS: dataInventory seeds 16 rows describing PLATFORM tables (users, audit_logs, llm_traces, kyc_documents). Is a tenant's register meant to describe the platform's processing, its own data, or both — and who owns editing it? legalBasis and retention are free text and must be constrained; the retention periods currently seeded ('Per KYC policy', '6 years', '90 days (6y for PHI access)') are legal determinations that must be confirmed by the business, never inferred here.

DPIA / AUTOMATED DECISIONS: both registers are create-only with no assessor, date, mitigations, reviewer or link to the system being assessed, and status (including 'Approved') is caller-supplied. What is the required review workflow and evidence?
RETENTION PURGE: RetentionPolicy promises a purge after keepForDays with a lastRun field nothing writes. Which job performs the purge, what does it purge, and what receipt proves it ran?

GUARDRAILS: five policies are seeded with ids minted by crypto.randomUUID() at module load (line 573), so their ids differ per tab and other screens match them by name instead. Are these platform-owned defaults with stable ids, or tenant-editable rows — and which component actually enforces them at Input/Output/Both?

CLIENT PORTAL AUTHZ: portalTabs and portalRoles describe what external partner users may see, but they live in the admin's own browser and enforce nothing. Where are portal users stored, how are roles assigned to them, and what is the permission model (the nested {read, comment, download, hidden[]} shape suggests per-tab field hiding)?
